title: Chapter 89 — Service, Retention & The Long Relationship
intro: The service partnership, retention saves, and the decade view.

sections.title: Service Is Revenue
sections.content:
The sale does not end at delivery. The CRM Warranty Follow-up stage is a revenue stage, not an admin stage. Registered, followed-up customers return for the second appliance. Laundry buyers become kitchen buyers. Single appliance buyers become package buyers.

Every service interaction is an opportunity to demonstrate care, earn trust, and set up the next sale.

sections.title: The Proactive Service Call
sections.content:
Do not wait for complaints. Call proactively. 48 hours post-delivery. 30 days post-delivery. At the water filter replacement interval — every 6 months for most fridges. At the one-year anniversary.

Each call is a retention touchpoint and a referral opportunity. 'Is everything still working great? Anything I can help with? By the way, if you know anyone shopping for appliances, I would love to help them.'

sections.title: The Angry Customer Is Your Best Opportunity
sections.content:
A customer who had a problem resolved well is MORE loyal than one who never had a problem. This is the Service Recovery Paradox — it is proven research, not wishful thinking.

When something goes wrong: let them vent without interrupting. Acknowledge their emotion. Take ownership. Solve it with a timeline and your name attached. Follow up before the deadline, even if you have no update. After resolution, offer something tangible — an accessory, a filter, a delivery credit.

The angry customer who becomes a fan is your best salesperson. They will tell everyone about how you fixed it.
